title: Canon gap (one row of the gap tracker)
description: One row of the gap tracker, the only write path agents have into the canon process. An agent that finds a missing, stale or conflicting fact files a row here instead of editing a page; humans triage it. Property names carry spaces because they are the column headers of templates/databases/canon-gaps.csv and the property names of the Notion database, so a CSV row or an API payload validates without renaming. Reference: docs/formats.md section 6 and templates/databases/schemas.md.
$comment: Suggested page must be either a canonical slug (a key of the governing contract's canonical_pages) or one of new_page, decision_log, unsure. The schema can only check the shape of a slug; the sync cross-checks the value against the contract so the database and the reporting skill cannot drift apart. Other rules that live in the skill, not the schema: dedup-check open rows for the same term or page before inserting; one row per gap; definitional failures route to glossary; confirm to the user with the row URL.

Gap.description: The title: one line, leading with the term or fact ('Customer count: README said 400+ while the sales storyboard said 350'). No line breaks; detail goes in Where it hurt.

Where it hurt.description: The task that failed or degraded, with a date ('Outbound email draft on 2026-09-26 cited both numbers in one paragraph; the draft was held'). The date lets triage judge urgency and lets a later reader find the run.

anyOf.description: new_page: no existing page should hold this. decision_log: an owner must decide, not document. unsure: the agent could not tell; a human routes it.
A canonical slug from the governing contract (company_readme, glossary, ...). Definitional failures route to glossary.

Suggested page.description: Where the fix belongs: a canonical slug, or new_page, decision_log or unsure. Validated against the contract's canonical_pages by the sync.

Status.description: Agents create rows as new and never change Status. Humans move a row to accepted (the gap is real and owned), patched (the page was fixed; cite the change log) or rejected (not a gap, with a reason in the row).

Reporter.description: Who filed it: a person, or 'Claude (<task>)' for autonomous runs ('Claude (outbound-draft)'). Naming the task makes recurring gaps from one skill visible.

Context link.description: URL of the canon page with the problem, or of the artifact where it surfaced. Triage opens this first; a row without a link is a rumour.

Reported.description: Created time, set automatically by the database. Optional in this schema because a CSV import row does not carry it; an exported row does.
